    STX .romSelectRegister                              ; switch the ROM into the memory map  $^$ 0xdc18
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdc1b



; ***************************************************************************************
; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Chapter 11: Interrupt processing
;
; ***************************************************************************************
; ***************************************************************************************

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; IRQ entry point
;
; On Entry:
;       The stack contains status register (flags); high and low bytes of previous program
;       counter.
;
; IRQ and BRK causes execution here. If it was a BRK instruction we branch (see .brkRoutine)
; otherwise we call (indirectly via IRQ1V) the default IRQ1 handler (see .irq1Handler)
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.irqEntryPoint
    STA .interruptAccumulator                           ; save A  $^$ 0xdc1c
    PLA                                                 ; read flags  $^$ 0xdc1e
    PHA                                                 ; store flags again  $^$ 0xdc1f
    AND #%00010000                                      ; check BRK flag  $^$ 0xdc20
    BNE .brkRoutine                                     ; if (BRK flag set) then branch (to BRK handler)  $^$ 0xdc22
    JMP (.vectorIRQ1V)                                  ; jump to the IRQ1 vector (by default this will jump to .irq1Handler)  $^$ 0xdc24

; ***************************************************************************************
.brkRoutine
    TXA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdc27
    PHA                                                 ; } save X on stack  $^$ 0xdc28
    TSX                                                 ; get stack pointer  $^$ 0xdc29
    LDA .stackPage + 3,X                                ; get program counter low  $^$ 0xdc2a
    CLD                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdc2d
    SEC                                                 ; set carry  $^$ 0xdc2e
    SBC #1                                              ; subtract 1  $^$ 0xdc2f
    STA .brkAddressLow                                  ; and store  $^$ 0xdc31
    LDA .stackPage + 4,X                                ; get high byte  $^$ 0xdc33
    SBC #0                                              ; subtract 1 if necessary  $^$ 0xdc36
    STA .brkAddressHigh                                 ; and store  $^$ 0xdc38
    LDA .currentlySelectedROM                           ; get currently active ROM  $^$ 0xdc3a
    STA .romNumberActiveLastBRK                         ; and store it  $^$ 0xdc3c
    STX .stackPointerLastBRK                            ; store stack pointer  $^$ 0xdc3f
    LDX #.romServiceCallBreakInstruction                ; }  $^$ 0xdc41
    JSR .osbyte143EntryPoint                            ; } issue ROM service call 6 (Break) to ROMs so they get a chance to respond.  $^$ 0xdc43
                                                        ; at this point .brkAddressLow/High points to the byte after the BRK instruction.
                                                        ; ROMS may use BRK for their own purposes

    LDX .languageROMNumber                              ; get current language  $^$ 0xdc46
    JSR .selectROM                                      ; and activate it  $^$ 0xdc49
    PLA                                                 ; get back original value of X  $^$ 0xdc4c
    TAX                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdc4d
    LDA .interruptAccumulator                           ; get back original value of A  $^$ 0xdc4e
    CLI                                                 ; allow interrupts  $^$ 0xdc50
    JMP (.vectorBRKV)                                   ; and JUMP via BRKV (normally into current language)  $^$ 0xdc51


; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Default BRK handler
;
; This is the default BRK handler that is used at boot time. When BASIC or other language
; ROM starts it will set up it's own BRK handler instead.
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.brkHandler
    LDY #0                                              ; Y=0 to point to byte after BRK  $^$ 0xdc54
    JSR .printMessage                                   ; print message  $^$ 0xdc56

    LDA .startupMessageSuppressionAndBootOptions        ; } bit 0 set means: lock up machine if !BOOT errors from DISC (because e.g. no language found)  $^$ 0xdc59
    ROR                                                 ; } rotate into carry  $^$ 0xdc5c
-
    BCS -                                               ; if (carry set) then branch (hang the machine!)  $^$ 0xdc5d

    JSR .OSNEWL                                         ; print two newlines  $^$ 0xdc5f
    JSR .OSNEWL                                         ;  $^$ 0xdc62
    JMP .setTapeFSAndFindLanguageROM                    ; set tape filing system before  $^$ 0xdc65
                                                        ; entering current language

; ***************************************************************************************
.rs423Handler
    SEC                                                 ; set carry  $^$ 0xdc68
    ROR .rs423ReadyFlag                                 ; set RS-423 ready  $^$ 0xdc69
    BIT .rs423ControlRegisterCopy                       ; check bit 7 of current ACIA control register (aka 'CR7' - ACIA interrupts enabled flag)  $^$ 0xdc6c
    BPL .rs423SetRequestToSendInactive                  ; if (ACIA interrupts disabled) then branch  $^$ 0xdc6f
    JSR .getRS423InputBufferFreeBytes                   ; call subroutine to check if serial buffer is full  $^$ 0xdc71
    LDX #0                                              ; set X to the value (zero) which will clear bit 5 and 6 of ACIA control register  $^$ 0xdc74
                                                        ; (aka 'CR5' and 'CR6' on the ACIA 6850 datasheet)
                                                        ; which means set the 'Request To Send' pin low and transmit interrupt disabled.
                                                        ; this is the active state.
    BCS .rs423BufferSpaceOK                             ; if (buffer has enough free space) then branch  $^$ 0xdc76

.rs423SetRequestToSendInactive
    LDX #%01000000                                      ; set X to value which will clear bit 5 and set bit 6 of ACIA control register  $^$ 0xdc78
                                                        ; (aka CR5 and CR6 on the ACIA 6850 datasheet)
                                                        ; which means set the 'Request To Send' pin high and transmit interrupt disabled.
                                                        ; this is the inactive state.
.rs423BufferSpaceOK
    JMP .writeToACIARequestToSend                       ; write to 'Request To Send' value in ACIA  $^$ 0xdc7a

; ***************************************************************************************
.readFromRS423
    LDY .acia6850DataRegister                           ; read serial data from ACIA  $^$ 0xdc7d
    AND #$3A                                            ; AND %0011 1010  $^$ 0xdc80
    BNE .rs423ErrorDetected                             ; if (not zero) then branch  $^$ 0xdc82
    LDX .rs423InputSuppressionFlag                      ; read RS-423 input suppression flag  $^$ 0xdc84
    BNE +                                               ; if (RS-423 input suppressed) then branch (return)  $^$ 0xdc87
    INX                                                 ; X=1  $^$ 0xdc89
    JSR .osbyte153EntryPoint                            ; put byte in RS-423 input buffer  $^$ 0xdc8a
    JSR .getRS423InputBufferFreeBytes                   ; count buffer  $^$ 0xdc8d
    BCC .rs423SetRequestToSendInactive                  ; if (buffer is low on free space) then branch back (to make 'Request To Send' inactive)  $^$ 0xdc90
+
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdc92

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; IRQ1 default handler
;
; When a hardware device generates an IRQ, this IRQ1 handler is executed (as the default
; handler, see .irqEntryPoint). After saving registers and a suitable return address on
; the stack, we check three hardware devices in turn, to see what needs attention:
;
;  1. Check for ACIA interrupt (see .irq1CheckACIA)
;       1a. updates RS-423 or Cassette then exit
;  2. Check for System VIA interrupt (see .irq1CheckSystemVIA)
;       2a. If VSYNC then update:
;               vsync counter
;               RS-423 counter
;               flashing colours
;               then exit
;       2b. If Timer 2 times out (Speech timer) (see .irq1CheckSystemVIASpeech)
;               update speech system (send speech data from speech buffer as needed)
;               then exit
;       2c. If Timer 1 times out (100Hz timer) (see .irq1CheckSystemVIA100HzTimer)
;           then update:
;               the clock
;               the countdown timer event
;               the INKEY timeout counter
;               sound
;               speech
;               ACIA
;               printer
;               keyboard
;               ADC conversion
;               then exit
;  3. Check for User VIA interrupt (see .irq1CheckUserVIA)
;       3a. updates a parallel printer then exit
;
;  Unrecognised interrupts are passed on to IRQ2V, allowing user code to process it.
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.irq1Handler
    CLD                                                 ; clear decimal flag  $^$ 0xdc93
    LDA .interruptAccumulator                           ; }  $^$ 0xdc94
    PHA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdc96
    TXA                                                 ; } push original A,X,Y register onto stack  $^$ 0xdc97
    PHA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdc98
    TYA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdc99
    PHA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdc9a

    LDA #>(.restoreRegistersAndReturnFromInterrupt-1)   ; }  $^$ 0xdc9b
    PHA                                                 ; } push return address onto stack  $^$ 0xdc9d
    LDA #<(.restoreRegistersAndReturnFromInterrupt-1)   ; } RTS will now exit to .restoreRegistersAndReturnFromInterrupt  $^$ 0xdc9e
    PHA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdca0
    CLV                                                 ; clear V flag (meaning: check the ACIA generated the interrupt)  $^$ 0xdca1
    ; fall through...

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Check for ACIA Interrupt or Update ACIA
;
; Two modes of operation (V CLEAR and V SET)
;
; On Entry:
;       V CLEAR means check that the ACIA generated the interrupt, and if so then update
;               the RS-423 or cassette as needed
;       V  SET  means just update the RS-423
.irq1CheckACIA
    LDA .acia6850StatusRegister                         ; get the ACIA status register  $^$ 0xdca2
    BVS +                                               ; if ('V SET') then branch (don't  $^$ 0xdca5
                                                        ; check the ACIA generated the
                                                        ; interrupt)
    BPL .irq1CheckSystemVIA                             ; if (ACIA didn't generate the  $^$ 0xdca7
                                                        ; interrupt) then branch (check the
                                                        ; next thing)
+
    LDX .rs423TimeoutCounter                            ; read RS-423 timeout counter  $^$ 0xdca9
    DEX                                                 ; decrement it  $^$ 0xdcab
    BMI .rs423HasControl                                ; if (timed out) then branch  $^$ 0xdcac
    BVS .exit13                                         ; if ('V SET') then branch (return)  $^$ 0xdcae
    JMP .updateACIA                                     ; update ACIA  $^$ 0xdcb0

; ***************************************************************************************
.rs423ErrorDetectedSetAY
    LDY .acia6850DataRegister                           ; read ACIA data  $^$ 0xdcb3
    ROL                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdcb6
    ASL                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdcb7
    ; fall through...

; ***************************************************************************************
.rs423ErrorDetected
    TAX                                                 ; X=status byte shifted right once  $^$ 0xdcb8
    TYA                                                 ; A=character received  $^$ 0xdcb9
    LDY #.eventRS423ErrorDetected                       ; Y=7  $^$ 0xdcba
    JMP .eventEntryPoint                                ; check and service EVENT 7 RS-423 error  $^$ 0xdcbc

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Send to RS-423 / Serial printer as needed
;
; If we have a non-empty RS-423 output buffer, then send the next byte, reset the RS-423
; timeout counter and exit.
;
; If we have a serial printer, update the printer buffer empty flag. If not empty then
; send the byte to the printer (and also reset the RS-423 timeout counter).
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.writeToACIA
    LDX #.bufferNumberRS423Output                       ; }  $^$ 0xdcbf
    JSR .osbyte145EntryPoint                            ; } read from RS-423 output buffer  $^$ 0xdcc1
    BCC +                                               ; if (buffer isn't empty) then branch forward  $^$ 0xdcc4

    ; RS-423 buffer empty
    LDA .printerDestination                             ; read printer destination  $^$ 0xdcc6
    CMP #2                                              ; is it serial printer?  $^$ 0xdcc9
    BNE .rs423Handler                                   ; if (not a serial printer) then branch (it must be RS-423)  $^$ 0xdccb

    ; serial printer
    INX                                                 ; X=3 (.bufferNumberPrinter)  $^$ 0xdccd
    JSR .osbyte145EntryPoint                            ; read printer buffer  $^$ 0xdcce
    ROR .printerBufferEmptyFlag                         ; update the empty flag (put carry into bit 7)  $^$ 0xdcd1
    BMI .rs423Handler                                   ; if (printer buffer is empty) then branch  $^$ 0xdcd4
+
    STA .acia6850DataRegister                           ; pass either printer or RS-423 data to ACIA  $^$ 0xdcd6
    LDA #$E7                                            ; } reset timeout counter to  $^$ 0xdcd9
    STA .rs423TimeoutCounter                            ; } count up 25 vsyncs (0.5 seconds)  $^$ 0xdcdb
.exit13
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdcdd

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Service RS-423 interrupt
;
; See NAUG Section 8.4 - Serial system interrupts, Page 126
;
; On Entry:
;       A = ACIA status byte
;
;       Two modes of operation:
;       V CLEAR - read from RS-423; handle DCD (Data Carrier Detect); write to RS-423;
;                 handle unrecognised interrupt
;       V SET   - handle DCD; write to RS-423
; ***************************************************************************************
.rs423HasControl
    AND .rs423IRQBitMask                                ; AND with ACIA bit mask (normally $FF)  $^$ 0xdcde
    LSR                                                 ; shift right to put bit 0 of ACIA status (receive interrupt) in carry  $^$ 0xdce1
    BCC +                                               ; if (not a receive interrupt) then branch (skip read)  $^$ 0xdce2
    BVS +                                               ; if (V SET mode) then branch (skip read)  $^$ 0xdce4
    LDY .rs423ControlRegisterCopy                       ; read copy of ACIA control register  $^$ 0xdce6
    BMI .readFromRS423                                  ; if (ACIA 6850 interrupts enabled) then branch  $^$ 0xdce9
+
    LSR                                                 ; shift,  put bit 1 of ACIA status into carry  $^$ 0xdceb
    ROR                                                 ; rotate, put bit 2 of ACIA status into carry  $^$ 0xdcec
    BCS .rs423ErrorDetectedSetAY                        ; if (Data Carrier Detected interrupt) then branch  $^$ 0xdced
    BMI .writeToACIA                                    ; if (ACIA status bit 1 is set) then branch (transmit interrupt)  $^$ 0xdcef
    BVS .exit13                                         ; if (V SET mode) then branch (exit)  $^$ 0xdcf1
    ; fall through...

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Unrecognised Interrupt
;
; When we have an interrupt that we don't understand, pass it to the ROMs to see if
; they can handle it. If not, then pass it on to the IRQ2 vector.
; ***************************************************************************************
.unrecognisedInterrupt
    LDX #.romServiceCallUnrecognisedInterrupt           ; }  $^$ 0xdcf3
    JSR .osbyte143EntryPoint                            ; } issue paged ROM service call for 'unrecognised interrupt'  $^$ 0xdcf5
    BEQ .exit13                                         ; if (a ROM recognises it) then branch (exit)  $^$ 0xdcf8
    PLA                                                 ; otherwise remove address from stack  $^$ 0xdcfa
    PLA                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdcfb
    PLA                                                 ; and restore Y, X, and A  $^$ 0xdcfc
    TAY                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdcfd
    PLA                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdcfe
    TAX                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdcff
    PLA                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdd00
    STA .interruptAccumulator                           ; .interruptAccumulator=A  $^$ 0xdd01
    JMP (.vectorIRQ2V)                                  ; and offer to the user via IRQ2V  $^$ 0xdd03

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Check for System VIA interrupt
;
; Check if the System VIA triggered the interrupt and deal with it.
; ***************************************************************************************
.irq1CheckSystemVIA
    LDA .systemVIAInterruptFlagRegister                 ; read system VIA interrupt flag register  $^$ 0xdd06
    BPL .irq1CheckUserVIA                               ; if (the System VIA has not caused interrupt) then branch (try the next thing)  $^$ 0xdd09

    AND .systemVIAIRQBitMask                            ; mask with VIA bit mask (normally $FF)  $^$ 0xdd0b
    AND .systemVIAInterruptEnableRegister               ; and interrupt enable register  $^$ 0xdd0e
    ROR                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdd11
    ROR                                                 ; } rotate right twice to check for IRQ 1 (vsync)  $^$ 0xdd12
    BCC .irq1CheckSystemVIASpeech                       ; if (not vsync) then branch (to check for speech)  $^$ 0xdd13

    ; vsync interrupt
    DEC .verticalSyncCounter                            ; decrement vertical sync counter  $^$ 0xdd15
    LDA .rs423TimeoutCounter                            ; A = RS-423 Timeout counter  $^$ 0xdd18
    BPL +                                               ; if (positive) then branch  $^$ 0xdd1a
    INC .rs423TimeoutCounter                            ; increment counter  $^$ 0xdd1c
+
    LDA .videoULAFlashingColourIntervalCount            ; load flash counter  $^$ 0xdd1e
    BEQ .doneFlashingColours                            ; if (flashing system is not in use) then branch  $^$ 0xdd21
    DEC .videoULAFlashingColourIntervalCount            ; decrement counter  $^$ 0xdd23
    BNE .doneFlashingColours                            ; if (not time for a colour to flash) then branch (to continue processing)  $^$ 0xdd26

    ; ready to flash colour
    LDX .videoULAFirstFlashingColourInterval            ; get mark period count in X  $^$ 0xdd28
    LDA .videoULAVideoControlRegisterCopy               ; current Video ULA control setting in A  $^$ 0xdd2b
    LSR                                                 ; shift bit 0 into C  $^$ 0xdd2e
    BCC .restoreAndFlipBit                              ; if (first colour is in effect) then branch  $^$ 0xdd2f

    LDX .videoULASecondFlashingColourInterval           ; get second colour period count in X  $^$ 0xdd31
.restoreAndFlipBit
    ROL                                                 ; restore bit  $^$ 0xdd34
    EOR #1                                              ; and invert it  $^$ 0xdd35
    JSR .setVideoULA                                    ; then set colour  $^$ 0xdd37
    STX .videoULAFlashingColourIntervalCount            ; reset the count until the next flash  $^$ 0xdd3a

.doneFlashingColours
    LDY #.eventStartOfVSync                             ; Y=event type: start of vsync  $^$ 0xdd3d
    JSR .eventEntryPoint                                ; call the event  $^$ 0xdd3f
    LDA #%00000010                                      ; A=bit set to clear the vsync interrupt flag  $^$ 0xdd42
    JMP .storeToSystemVIAIFR                            ; clear interrupt and exit  $^$ 0xdd44


; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Check for User VIA interrupt
;
; Check if the User VIA triggered the interrupt and deal with it (check for parallel
; printer in particular).
; ***************************************************************************************
.irq1CheckUserVIA
    LDA .userVIAInterruptFlagRegister                   ; check User VIA interrupt flags register  $^$ 0xdd47
    BPL .unrecognisedInterrupt                          ; if (User VIA did not call interrupt) then branch  $^$ 0xdd4a

    AND .userVIAIRQBitMask                              ; }  $^$ 0xdd4c
    AND .userVIAInterruptEnableRegister                 ; }  $^$ 0xdd4f
    ROR                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdd52
    ROR                                                 ; } check for User IRQ bit 1 set (printer interrupt)  $^$ 0xdd53
    BCC .unrecognisedInterrupt                          ; if (not printer interrupt) then branch  $^$ 0xdd54
    LDY .printerDestination                             ; get printer type  $^$ 0xdd56
    DEY                                                 ; decrement  $^$ 0xdd59
    BNE .unrecognisedInterrupt                          ; if (not a parallel printer) then branch  $^$ 0xdd5a

    ; deal with parallel printer
    LDA #%00000010                                      ; interrupt bit 1 (printer interrupt)  $^$ 0xdd5c
    STA .userVIAInterruptFlagRegister                   ; clear interrupt bit 1  $^$ 0xdd5e
    STA .userVIAInterruptEnableRegister                 ; enable interrupt bit 1  $^$ 0xdd61
    LDX #.bufferNumberPrinter                           ; }  $^$ 0xdd64
    JMP .openPrinterChannel                             ; } output data to parallel printer  $^$ 0xdd66

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Check to see if the interrupt is a Speech interrupt and deal with it
;
; The speech processor chip has an internal 16 byte buffer to hold incoming data.
;
; When speaking, this buffer will run out every 50 milliseconds. When the buffer becomes
; half full, an interrupt occurs. In fact, a speech interrupt is generated when any of the
; following occur:
;
;   (1) End of speech processing
;   (2) Speech hardware is low on data (half full, i.e. 8 bytes or less), indicating more
;       phrase data needs to be supplied for the Speak External command.
;   (3) Speech hardware is empty of data, indicating the CPU failed to supply phrase data
;       fast enough for the Speak External command.
;   (4) At the start of a Speak External instruction, if speech hardware is not empty of data.
;
; We call .updateSpeech in the 100Hz interrupt to keep the speech hardware regularly supplied
; with data.
;
; On Entry:
;       A = System VIA interrupt flag shifted right twice
; ***************************************************************************************
.irq1CheckSystemVIASpeech
    ROL                                                 ; } rotate left twice to get back to  $^$ 0xdd69
    ROL                                                 ; } original interrupt flag register  $^$ 0xdd6a
                                                        ; } alignment of bits

    ROL                                                 ; rotate left to get bit 5 into bit 6  $^$ 0xdd6b
    ROL                                                 ; rotate left to get bit 6 into bit 7  $^$ 0xdd6c
    BPL .irq1CheckSystemVIA100HzTimer                   ; if (bit 5 of system via IFR is  $^$ 0xdd6d
                                                        ; clear, i.e. it's not timer 2, used
                                                        ; for the speech interrupt)
                                                        ; then branch

    ; deal with speech
    LDA #%00100000                                      ; } clear bit 5, the timer 2  $^$ 0xdd6f
    LDX #0                                              ; } interrupt  $^$ 0xdd71
    STA .systemVIAInterruptFlagRegister                 ; }  $^$ 0xdd73
    STX .systemVIATimer2CounterHigh                     ; clear Timer 2 (write to high byte)  $^$ 0xdd76

.updateSpeech
    LDX #8                                              ; } loop counter (shifted right on  $^$ 0xdd79
    STX .tempStoreFB                                    ; } each loop iteration)  $^$ 0xdd7b

    ; on each speech update we loop a maximum of 4 times to feed the speech chip with up to
    ; 4 bytes of new data from the CPU's speech buffer.
.feedSpeechChipWithDataLoop
    ; check our speech buffer, see if there's more data
    JSR .osbyte152EntryPoint                            ; examine buffer status for buffer 8  $^$ 0xdd7d
                                                        ; (the speech buffer), C set if buffer
                                                        ; is empty, otherwise A is byte read.
    ROR .speechBufferEmptyFlag                          ; shift carry into bit 7 - store as  $^$ 0xdd80
                                                        ; the 'speech buffer empty' bit
    BMI .exit14                                         ; if (top bit is set, i.e. set buffer  $^$ 0xdd83
                                                        ; is empty) then branch (return)
    TAY                                                 ; Y = A = next byte to be removed  $^$ 0xdd85
                                                        ; from speech buffer
    BEQ +                                               ;  $^$ 0xdd86

    ; check if speech chip is ready?
    JSR .osbyte158EntryPoint                            ; read byte from speech chip  $^$ 0xdd88
    BMI .exit14                                         ; if (top bit set) then branch (exit)  $^$ 0xdd8b

+
    ; read three bytes from the speech buffer: <ROM number> <2 byte address>
    JSR .osbyte145EntryPoint                            ; read a byte from CPU's speech buffer  $^$ 0xdd8d
    STA .currentSpeechPHROMOrROMNumber                  ; store ROM number  $^$ 0xdd90
    JSR .osbyte145EntryPoint                            ; read another byte  $^$ 0xdd92
    STA .romAddressHigh                                 ; store ROM address  $^$ 0xdd95
    JSR .osbyte145EntryPoint                            ; read another byte  $^$ 0xdd97
    STA .romAddressLow                                  ; store ROM address  $^$ 0xdd9a

    LDY .currentSpeechPHROMOrROMNumber                  ; Y=ROM / PHROM number  $^$ 0xdd9c
    BEQ .writeROMAddressToSpeechProcessor               ; if (current logical speech PHROM  $^$ 0xdd9e
                                                        ; or ROMFS Number is zero) then branch
    BPL .writeCommandAndAddressToSpeechProcessor        ; if (+ve) then branch  $^$ 0xdda0
    BIT .currentSpeechPHROMOrROMNumber                  ; check bit 6 of PHROM or ROM number  $^$ 0xdda2
    BVS +                                               ; if (PHROM or ROM number has bit 6  $^$ 0xdda4
                                                        ; set) then branch
    JSR .writeAddressAndROMNumberToSpeechProcessor      ; continue for more speech processing  $^$ 0xdda6
    BVC .enableOrDisableSpeech                          ; ALWAYS branch  $^$ 0xdda9

+
    ASL .romAddressLow                                  ; double ROM address  $^$ 0xddab
    ROL .romAddressHigh                                 ;  $^$ 0xddad
    JSR .readFromPHROM                                  ; and call .readFromPHROM  $^$ 0xddaf

.enableOrDisableSpeech
    LDY .speechSuppressionStatus                        ; get speech enable/disable flag  $^$ 0xddb2
                                                        ; whose values equate to speech
                                                        ; processor commands:
                                                        ; $50 = 'speak'; $20 = 'nop'
    JMP .osbyte159EntryPoint                            ; write to speech processor  $^$ 0xddb5

.writeCommandAndAddressToSpeechProcessor
    JSR .osbyte159EntryPoint                            ; write ROM number  $^$ 0xddb8
.writeROMAddressToSpeechProcessor
    LDY .romAddressLow                                  ; get address pointer in Y  $^$ 0xddbb
    JSR .osbyte159EntryPoint                            ; write address to speech chip  $^$ 0xddbd
    LDY .romAddressHigh                                 ; get address pointer high in Y  $^$ 0xddc0
    JSR .osbyte159EntryPoint                            ; write address to speech chip  $^$ 0xddc2

    LSR .tempStoreFB                                    ; update loop counter  $^$ 0xddc5
    BNE .feedSpeechChipWithDataLoop                     ; loop back  $^$ 0xddc7

.exit14
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xddc9


; ***************************************************************************************
;
; IRQ1 Interrupt - 100Hz interrupt
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.irq1CheckSystemVIA100HzTimer
    BCC .irq1CheckSystemVIAADCEndConversion             ; bit 6 is in carry. if (there is no bit 6 interrupt) then branch  $^$ 0xddca
    LDA #%01000000                                      ; }  $^$ 0xddcc
    STA .systemVIAInterruptFlagRegister                 ; } clear interrupt 6  $^$ 0xddce

    ; Update the 5 byte clock. There are 2 clock stores, at .timeClockA and .timeClockB. These
    ; are updated by adding 1 to the current clock and storing the result in the other, the
    ; direction of transfer being changed each time of update.  This ensures that at least
    ; 1 clock store is valid at any call as the current clock is only read.  Other methods
    ; would cause inaccuracies if a clock was read whilst being updated.
    LDA .timeClockSwitch                                ; get current system clock pointer (5 or 10)  $^$ 0xddd1
    TAX                                                 ; put old system clock pointer in X  $^$ 0xddd4
    EOR #$0F                                            ; invert bits so it toggles between 5 and 10  $^$ 0xddd5
    PHA                                                 ; remember A  $^$ 0xddd7
    TAY                                                 ; put new system clock pointer in Y  $^$ 0xddd8
-
    LDA .timeClockA-1,X                                 ; get current system clock value  $^$ 0xddd9
    ADC #0                                              ; increment it (carry is set on the first iteration of the loop,  $^$ 0xdddc
                                                        ;     thereafter carry is set as needed based on this increment)
    STA .timeClockA-1,Y                                 ; store result in new copy  $^$ 0xddde
    DEX                                                 ; decrement X  $^$ 0xdde1
    BEQ +                                               ; if (finished) then branch (loop ends)  $^$ 0xdde2
    DEY                                                 ; decrement Y  $^$ 0xdde4
    BNE -                                               ; and go back and do next byte  $^$ 0xdde5
+
    PLA                                                 ; get back new clock pointer  $^$ 0xdde7
    STA .timeClockSwitch                                ; and store back in clock pointer  $^$ 0xdde8

    ; Update countdown interval timer. An EVENT is generated when it times out.
    LDX #5                                              ; set loop counter  $^$ 0xddeb
-
    INC .countdownIntervalTimer - 1,X                   ; increment byte for countdown timer  $^$ 0xdded
    BNE +                                               ; if (done updating timer bytes) then branch  $^$ 0xddf0
    DEX                                                 ; decrement loop counter  $^$ 0xddf2
    BNE -                                               ; if (not finished looping) do it again  $^$ 0xddf3

    LDY #.eventIntervalTimerCrossingZero                ; at this point all the interval timer bytes are zero  $^$ 0xddf5
    JSR .eventEntryPoint                                ; call EVENT 5 interval timer  $^$ 0xddf7

    ; Update INKEY timeout. Used when reading a key within a time limit.
+
    LDA .inkeyTimeoutCounterLow                         ; get low byte of inkey countdown timer  $^$ 0xddfa
    BNE +                                               ; if (inkey timer is non-zero) then branch forward  $^$ 0xddfd
    LDA .inkeyTimeoutCounterHigh                        ; get high byte of inkey countdown timer  $^$ 0xddff
    BEQ ++                                              ; if (inkey timer is zero) then branch forward  $^$ 0xde02
    DEC .inkeyTimeoutCounterHigh                        ; decrement high byte  $^$ 0xde04
+
    DEC .inkeyTimeoutCounterLow                         ; and decrement low byte  $^$ 0xde07

    ; Update sound.
++
    BIT .soundIsUpdatingFlag                            ; check bit 7 of sound flag  $^$ 0xde0a
                                                        ; (this bit is set while processing
                                                        ; sound interrupt. check so we don't
                                                        ; try to process a second sound
                                                        ; interrupt while still processing
                                                        ; the first)
    BPL +                                               ; if (bit clear; still processing)  $^$ 0xde0d
                                                        ; then branch (skip forward)
    INC .soundIsUpdatingFlag                            ; increment to 0 (to signify that  $^$ 0xde0f
                                                        ; sound is being processed here)
    CLI                                                 ; allow interrupts briefly  $^$ 0xde12
    JSR .processSoundInterrupt                          ; process sound  $^$ 0xde13
    SEI                                                 ; disable interrupts  $^$ 0xde16
    DEC .soundIsUpdatingFlag                            ; decrement 'sound is updating' flag  $^$ 0xde17
                                                        ; back to $FF (this signifies that we
                                                        ; are done processing the sound)

    ; Update speech.
+
    BIT .speechBufferEmptyFlag                          ; check speech buffer empty flag  $^$ 0xde1a
    BMI +                                               ; if (speech buffer is empty) then  $^$ 0xde1d
                                                        ; branch (skip speech)
    JSR .osbyte158EntryPoint                            ; read speech processor status register  $^$ 0xde1f
    EOR #%10100000                                      ; flip two bits  $^$ 0xde22
    CMP #%01100000                                      ; check  $^$ 0xde24
    BCC +                                               ; if (result < $60) then branch  $^$ 0xde26
    JSR .updateSpeech                                   ; process speech  $^$ 0xde28

    ; Update ACIA.
+
    BIT .allBitsSet                                     ; set V flag  $^$ 0xde2b
    JSR .irq1CheckACIA                                  ; update ACIA  $^$ 0xde2e

    ; Update keyboard.
    LDA .lastKeyPressedInternal                         ; } check if a key is currently  $^$ 0xde31
    ORA .firstKeyPressedInternal                        ; } pressed  $^$ 0xde33
    AND .enableKeyboardInterruptProcessingFlag          ; ignore key presses if the flag  $^$ 0xde35
                                                        ; is zero
    BEQ +                                               ; if (no key pressed or we should  $^$ 0xde38
                                                        ; ignore keys pressed) then branch
                                                        ; (ignore keyboard)
    SEC                                                 ; set carry  $^$ 0xde3a
    JSR .keyboardInterruptRoutine                       ; handle keyboard interrupt  $^$ 0xde3b

    ; Update printer.
+
    JSR .printerServiceCallIfNotEmpty                   ; check for data in printer buffer  $^$ 0xde3e

    ; Update ADC conversion.
    BIT .adcDataStatusRegister                          ; check ADC status register  $^$ 0xde41
    BVS .handleADCConversionEnds                        ; if (bit 6 is set, i.e. ADC not  $^$ 0xde44
                                                        ; busy) then branch

    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xde46


; ***************************************************************************************
;
; IRQ1 Interrupt - Analogue to Digital Conversion (End of Conversion)
;
; See .osbyte17EntryPoint
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.irq1CheckSystemVIAADCEndConversion
    ROL                                                 ; put original bit 4 from .systemVIAInterruptFlagRegister into bit 7 of A  $^$ 0xde47
    BPL .irq1CheckSystemVIAKeyboard                     ; if (not an ADC conversion interrupt) then branch  $^$ 0xde48

.handleADCConversionEnds
    LDX .adcCurrentChannel                              ; get current ADC channel  $^$ 0xde4a
    BEQ .clearInterrupt4                                ; if (zero) then branch (clear interrupt and exit)  $^$ 0xde4d

    LDA .adcDataLowByte                                 ; read low data byte  $^$ 0xde4f
    STA .lowByteLastByteFromADCChannel1 - 1,X           ; store it in memory  $^$ 0xde52
    LDA .adcDataHighByte                                ; get high data byte  $^$ 0xde55
    STA .highByteLastByteFromADCChannel1 - 1,X          ; and store it in high byte  $^$ 0xde58
    STX .adcLastChannelRead                             ; store last ADC channel read  $^$ 0xde5b
    LDY #.eventADCConversionComplete                    ; handle event 3 conversion complete  $^$ 0xde5e
    JSR .eventEntryPoint                                ;  $^$ 0xde60

    DEX                                                 ; decrement X  $^$ 0xde63
    BNE +                                               ; if (X != 0) then branch forward  $^$ 0xde64
    LDX .maximumADCChannelNumber                        ; get highest ADC channel present  $^$ 0xde66
+
    JSR .startADCConversion                             ; start new conversion  $^$ 0xde69
.clearInterrupt4
    LDA #%00010000                                      ; reset interrupt 4  $^$ 0xde6c
.storeToSystemVIAIFR
    STA .systemVIAInterruptFlagRegister                 ;  $^$ 0xde6e
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xde71

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; IRQ1 Interrupt - keyboard
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.irq1CheckSystemVIAKeyboard
    ROL                                                 ; get original bit 0 in bit 7 position  $^$ 0xde72
    ROL                                                 ;  $^$ 0xde73
    ROL                                                 ;  $^$ 0xde74
    ROL                                                 ;  $^$ 0xde75
    BPL +                                               ; if (not a keyboard interrupt) then branch (skip keyboard processing)  $^$ 0xde76
    JSR .keyboardInterruptRoutine                       ; scan keyboard  $^$ 0xde78
    LDA #%00000001                                      ; }  $^$ 0xde7b
    BNE .storeToSystemVIAIFR                            ; } reset interrupt 0 and return  $^$ 0xde7d
+
    JMP .unrecognisedInterrupt                          ;  $^$ 0xde7f

; ***************************************************************************************
.restoreRegistersAndReturnFromInterrupt
    PLA                                                 ; restore AXY registers  $^$ 0xde82
    TAY                                                 ;  $^$ 0xde83
    PLA                                                 ;  $^$ 0xde84
    TAX                                                 ;  $^$ 0xde85
    PLA                                                 ;  $^$ 0xde86
    STA .interruptAccumulator                           ; store A  $^$ 0xde87
    ; fall through...

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Default IRQ2 handler - does nothing
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.irq2Handler
    LDA .interruptAccumulator                           ; get back original value of A  $^$ 0xde89
    RTI                                                 ; return  $^$ 0xde8b

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; OSBYTE 17 - Start ADC conversions
;
; See 7002.png
;
; Analogue to digital conversion is performed by the ADC 7002 chip. It has four channels
; of data that can be read. This is often used to read an analogue joystick. This starts
; the conversion happening. They will keep happening until OSBYTE 16 with X=0 is called.
;
; OSBYTE 16 selects the range of channels to convert (0-4). See .osbyte16EntryPoint.
;
; OSBYTE 190 selects the ADC conversion type (8 or 12 bits). See .adcConversionType.
; Twelve bit conversion is the default (which takes about 10ms). Eight bit conversions are
; faster at around 4ms.
;
; The ADC 7002 generates an interrupt when the conversion is complete, and the IRQ1 handler
; stores the two byte result (in .lowByteLastByteFromADCChannel1 and upwards). It also
; starts the next conversion. See .irq1CheckSystemVIAADCEndConversion.
;
; OSBYTE 128 reads the latest converted ADC value (X=ADC channel 1-4). See .osbyte128EntryPoint.
; OSBYTE 128 can also read the state of the fire buttons. (X=0). See .osbyte128EntryPoint.
; These are encapsulated in the BASIC ADVAL command.
;
; On Entry:
;       X = ADC channel number (1-4)
;       Y = 0
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.osbyte17EntryPoint
    STY .adcLastChannelRead                             ; set last channel to finish conversion (to zero)  $^$ 0xde8c
.startADCConversion
    CPX #5                                              ;  $^$ 0xde8f
    BCC +                                               ; if (X < 5) then branch (skip forward)  $^$ 0xde91
    LDX #4                                              ; X=4 (maximum)  $^$ 0xde93
+
    STX .adcCurrentChannel                              ; store it as current ADC channel  $^$ 0xde95
    LDY .adcConversionType                              ; get conversion type  $^$ 0xde98
    DEY                                                 ; decrement  $^$ 0xde9b
    TYA                                                 ; A=Y  $^$ 0xde9c
    AND #%00001000                                      ; clear to zero except for bit 3 set  $^$ 0xde9d
                                                        ; indicates a 12 bit conversion
    CLC                                                 ; } add the ADC channel (1-4)  $^$ 0xde9f
    ADC .adcCurrentChannel                              ; } then subtract one, effectively  $^$ 0xdea0
    SBC #0                                              ; } adding channel (0-3) into bits 0-2  $^$ 0xdea3
    STA .adcStartConversionRegister                     ; store value to start ADC conversion  $^$ 0xdea5
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdea8

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Display string on screen
;
; Display the boot message (e.g. 'BBC Computer 32K') and language ROM title (e.g. 'BASIC')
;
; On Entry:
;       Y = offset from page of .vduBaseAddress to start of string -1
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.displayString
    LDA #>.vduBaseAddress                               ; Start of string area (high byte)  $^$ 0xdea9
.displayStringAY
    STA .displayStringAddressHigh                       ; store it  $^$ 0xdeab
    LDA #0                                              ; Low byte is zero (we use Y to index to correct string)  $^$ 0xdead
    STA .displayStringAddressLow                        ; store it and start loop  $^$ 0xdeaf
    ; fall through...

; ***************************************************************************************
.printMessage
    INY                                                 ; print character in string  $^$ 0xdeb1
    LDA (.displayStringAddressLow),Y                    ; pointed to by $FD/E  $^$ 0xdeb2
    JSR .OSASCI                                         ; print it expanding Carriage returns  $^$ 0xdeb4
    TAX                                                 ; store A in X  $^$ 0xdeb7
    BNE .printMessage                                   ; and loop again if not zero  $^$ 0xdeb8
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdeba

; ***************************************************************************************
; On Entry:
;       X/Y holds the time limit
.osbyte129Timed
    STX .inkeyTimeoutCounterLow                         ; store time in INKEY countdown timer  $^$ 0xdebb
    STY .inkeyTimeoutCounterHigh                        ; which is decremented every 10ms  $^$ 0xdebe
    LDA #255                                            ;  $^$ 0xdec1
    BNE .readCharacterTimed                             ; ALWAYS branch  $^$ 0xdec3

; ***************************************************************************************
; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Chapter 12: Command Line Interpreter (star commands)
;
; ***************************************************************************************
; ***************************************************************************************

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Introduction
;
; The Command Line Interpreter is responsible for executing star commands. There are a number
; built in to the system (see .starCommandTable), and more can be added via paged ROMs.
;
; The commands can have parameters as integer decimal, hexadecimal values, and strings.
; These commands have characters in the range 32-126, but can encode control codes and other
; non-printable characters. It uses GSINIT and GSREAD to convert the set of ASCII printable
; string characters into a full 8-bit ASCII converted values. See .gsinitEntryPoint .
;
; This chapter contains integer (in string form) to byte conversion,
; see .parseDecimalNumberFromString. A conversion for a hex digit in string form to a byte,
; see .readHexDigit, which is used to read a wole 32 bit address, see .readOSFILEAddress .
;
; Historical note: Every Acorn computer from the System 2 onwards has a CLI, and the
; asterisk probably derives from the System 2's use of it as a prompt character.
;
; ***************************************************************************************

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; OSRDCH - Read a character
;       This reads from an EXEC file if open, or the current input buffer otherwise
;
; On Entry:
;       A = 0 for reading a key instantly
;       A = 255 for reading a key with a time limit
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.osrdchEntryPoint
    LDA #0                                              ;  $^$ 0xdec5
.readCharacterTimed
    STA .readCharacterTimedFlag                         ; store A (0 or 255) to indicate if it's a timed read  $^$ 0xdec7
    TXA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdec9
    PHA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdeca
    TYA                                                 ; } store X and Y  $^$ 0xdecb
    PHA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdecc
    LDY .execFileHandle                                 ; get *EXEC file handle  $^$ 0xdecd
    BEQ .readCharacterFromCurrentInputBufferLoop        ; if (zero, i.e. no EXEC file open) then branch  $^$ 0xded0

    ; read from an EXEC file
    SEC                                                 ; set carry  $^$ 0xded2
    ROR .tapeCritical                                   ; set bit 7 of tape filing system active flag to prevent clashes  $^$ 0xded3
    JSR .OSBGET                                         ; get a byte from the file  $^$ 0xded5
    PHP                                                 ; push flags to preserve carry  $^$ 0xded8
    LSR .tapeCritical                                   ; clear .tapeCritical flag  $^$ 0xded9
    PLP                                                 ; get back flags  $^$ 0xdedb
    BCC .pullAndReturn                                  ; if (character found) then branch (recall values and exit)  $^$ 0xdedc
    LDA #0                                              ; error reading from file, so close the file  $^$ 0xdede
    STA .execFileHandle                                 ; store it in exec file handle  $^$ 0xdee0
    JSR .OSFIND                                         ; and close file via OSFIND  $^$ 0xdee3

.readCharacterFromCurrentInputBufferLoop
    BIT .escapeFlag                                     ; check ESCAPE flag  $^$ 0xdee6
    BMI .setEscapeConditionAndExit                      ; if (ESCAPE flag set) then branch (set escape condition and exit)  $^$ 0xdee8
    LDX .currentInputBuffer                             ; get current input buffer number  $^$ 0xdeea
    JSR .readFromEconetOrSoftKeyOrInputBufferA          ; get a byte from current input buffer  $^$ 0xdeed
    BCC .pullAndReturn                                  ; if (valid character found) then branch (exit)  $^$ 0xdef0

.checkForTiming
    BIT .readCharacterTimedFlag                         ; check for timed read  $^$ 0xdef2
    BVC .readCharacterFromCurrentInputBufferLoop        ; if (this is not timed) then branch (go back and read byte from input buffer again)  $^$ 0xdef4
    LDA .inkeyTimeoutCounterLow                         ; check timers  $^$ 0xdef6
    ORA .inkeyTimeoutCounterHigh                        ;  $^$ 0xdef9
    BNE .readCharacterFromCurrentInputBufferLoop        ; if (timer is not zero) then branch (loop back and keep trying to read)  $^$ 0xdefc
    BCS +                                               ; if (timed out) then branch (exit without storing character read)  $^$ 0xdefe

.setEscapeConditionAndExit
    SEC                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdf00
    LDA #.charESCAPE                                    ; ESCAPE character read  $^$ 0xdf01

.pullAndReturn
    STA .readCharacterTimedFlag                         ; remember character read  $^$ 0xdf03
+
    PLA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdf05
    TAY                                                 ; } restore X,Y  $^$ 0xdf06
    PLA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdf07
    TAX                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xdf08
    LDA .readCharacterTimedFlag                         ; recall character read  $^$ 0xdf09
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdf0b

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Copyright string
; Only used as part of the check for valid Paged ROM, never printed
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.copyrightString
    !text ")C(",0                                       ; Copyright string (backwards)

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Star command table
;
; *. <directory>                Synonym of *CAT
; *FX <a>,<x>,<y>               Calls OSBYTE
; *BASIC                        Start BASIC
; *CAT <directory>              Show catalogue from filing system
; *CODE <x>,<y>                 Execute code via USERV with A=0
; *EXEC <filename>              Execute a script file
; *HELP <string>                Get help
; *KEY <n> <string>             Define a soft key definition
; *LINE <string>                Execute code via USERV with A=1
; *LOAD <filename> <addr>       Load file
; *MOTOR <n>                    Turn on/off cassette motor
; *OPT <x>,<y>                  Set filing system options (Equivalent to OSBYTE 139)
; *RUN <filename>               Load and execute a file from the current filing system
; *ROM                          Set ROM filing system
; *SAVE <filename> <start> <end> <exec> <load> Save memory to the current filing system
; *SPOOL <filename>             Save keystrokes to the current filing system
; *TAPE <n>                     Set the TAPE filing system
; *TV <x>,<y>                   Adjust the TV display
;
; Commands can be abbreviated, e.g. *M. for *MOTOR.
;
; This list is not quite alphabetical, so that short abbreviations yield the more common
; commands, so *LOAD comes before *LINE so that *L. becomes *LOAD; and *R. becomes *RUN,
; not *ROM.
;
; The last entry is empty to catch anything else.
;
; After the name and address of each command is a single byte parameter that is passed in
; the accumulator before calling the routine's address. If the parameter has the top bit
; clear (*.; *BASIC; *CAT; *EXEC; *LOAD; *LINE; *RUN; *SAVE; *SPOOL), then the next part of
; the command line is decoded into a string (usually a pathname).
;
; A group of commands (*CODE; *MOTOR; *OPT; *TAPE; *ROM; *TV) are synonyms for *FX calls
; with the parameter being the OSBYTE number.
;
; Historical note: The Acorn System 2 star commands were *BASIC, *CAT, *LOAD, *SAVE, *GO,
; *RUN, *MEM, *MON, *NOMON, *DRIVE, *USE, and *FLOAD, while the Atom provided *CAT, *LOAD,
; *SAVE, *RUN, *MON, *NOMON, *FLOAD, and *DOS. Their CLIs each provide the dot abbreviation
; and have similar command-parsing code. But the System 2 and Atom monitors lack the ability
; to EXEC scripts, and have no comment notation. *FLOAD, "finish loading", allowed part of
; a file to be loaded into memory by ignoring its block numbers -- an ability which was,
; perhaps wisely, dropped from the BBC.
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.starCommandTable
    !text "."                                           ; command name
    !be16 .passToCurrentFilingSystem                    ; address of routine to call
    !byte 5                                             ; parameter to routine (in A)

    !text "FX"
    !be16 .fxEntryPoint
    !byte $FF

    !text "BASIC"
    !be16 .basicEntryPoint
    !byte 0

    !text "CAT"
    !be16 .passToCurrentFilingSystem
    !byte 5

    !text "CODE"
    !be16 .starCommandsForSpecificOSBYTEs
    !byte $88

    !text "EXEC"
    !be16 .closeAndOptionallyOpenANewEXECFile
    !byte 0

    !text "HELP"
    !be16 .starHelp
    !byte $FF

    !text "KEY"
    !be16 .starKey
    !byte $FF

    !text "LOAD"
    !be16 .starLoad
    !byte 0

    !text "LINE"
    !be16 .uservJumper
    !byte 1

    !text "MOTOR"
    !be16 .starCommandsForSpecificOSBYTEs
    !byte $89

    !text "OPT"
    !be16 .starCommandsForSpecificOSBYTEs
    !byte $8B

    !text "RUN"
    !be16 .passToCurrentFilingSystem
    !byte 4

    !text "ROM"
    !be16 .starCommandsForSpecificOSBYTEs
    !byte $8D

    !text "SAVE"
    !be16 .starLoadSave
    !byte 0

    !text "SPOOL"
    !be16 .starSpool
    !byte 0

    !text "TAPE"
    !be16 .starCommandsForSpecificOSBYTEs
    !byte $8C

    !text "TV"
    !be16 .starCommandsForSpecificOSBYTEs
    !byte $90

    !text ""
    !be16 .passToCurrentFilingSystem
    !byte 3
    !byte 0


; ***************************************************************************************
;
; OSCLI - Command Line Interpreter
;       the default handler for CLIV vector
;
; On Entry:
;       XY is the address of the command line (terminated with a carriage return)
;
; On Exit:
;       A,X,Y,Flags undefined
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.oscliEntryPoint
    STX .stringInputBufferAddressLow                    ; Store XY in .stringInputBufferAddressLow/High  $^$ 0xdf89
    STY .stringInputBufferAddressHigh                   ;  $^$ 0xdf8b
    LDA #8                                              ;  $^$ 0xdf8d
    JSR .passToCurrentFilingSystem                      ; Inform filing system CLI being processed  $^$ 0xdf8f
    LDY #0                                              ; loop counter  $^$ 0xdf92
-
    LDA (.stringInputBufferAddressLow),Y                ; Check the line is correctly terminated  $^$ 0xdf94
    CMP #.charRETURN                                    ; loop until CR is found  $^$ 0xdf96
    BEQ .stringOK                                       ;  $^$ 0xdf98
    INY                                                 ; move to next character  $^$ 0xdf9a
    BNE -                                               ; loop back if less than 256 bytes long  $^$ 0xdf9b
    RTS                                                 ; string is > 255 characters, so return  $^$ 0xdf9d

    ; String is terminated ok - now skip prepended spaces and '*'s
.stringOK
    LDY #$FF                                            ; Y = offset into string (which is about to be incremented so it will start at zero)  $^$ 0xdf9e
-
    JSR .incAndSkipSpaces                               ; Skip any spaces  $^$ 0xdfa0
    BEQ .exit15                                         ; if (CR found) then branch (return)  $^$ 0xdfa3
    CMP #.charSTAR                                      ; check for '*'  $^$ 0xdfa5
    BEQ -                                               ; if ('*' found) then branch (Loop back to skip it and skip spaces again)  $^$ 0xdfa7

    JSR .skipSpacesAndCheckForCRInStringInput           ; doesn't need to move forward, but checks if the current character is CR  $^$ 0xdfa9
    BEQ .exit15                                         ; if (CR found) then branch (exit)  $^$ 0xdfac
    CMP #.charBAR                                       ; check for '|' (a comment)  $^$ 0xdfae
    BEQ .exit15                                         ; if ('|' found) then branch (exit)  $^$ 0xdfb0
    CMP #.charFORWARDSLASH                              ; check for '/'  $^$ 0xdfb2
    BNE .startLookingForCommand                         ; if (NOT forward slash) then branch forward  $^$ 0xdfb4
    INY                                                 ; Move past the '/'  $^$ 0xdfb6
    JSR .convertStringInputPointerToXY                  ; Convert the address (.stringInputBufferAddressLow/High + Y) into XY  $^$ 0xdfb7
    LDA #2                                              ; 2 = execute "*/" command (See NAUG Section 16.1.7 - FSCV, Page 256-7)  $^$ 0xdfba
    BNE .passToCurrentFilingSystem                      ; ALWAYS branch (call into current filing system service routine)  $^$ 0xdfbc

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Start looking for command
;
; Look command up in command table
; ***************************************************************************************
.startLookingForCommand
    STY .currentStringPointer                           ; Store offset to start of command in command line  $^$ 0xdfbe
    LDX #0                                              ; start of command  $^$ 0xdfc0
    BEQ .lookForCommand                                 ; ALWAYS branch  $^$ 0xdfc2

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Compare character in A in a star command
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.compareCharacterInCommand
    EOR .starCommandTable,X                             ; compare with character from star command table  $^$ 0xdfc4
    AND #%11011111                                      ; ignore case (zero the bit that distinguishes between upper and lower case)  $^$ 0xdfc7
    BNE .namesDontMatch                                 ; if (no match) then branch  $^$ 0xdfc9
    INY                                                 ; increment offset in command line  $^$ 0xdfcb
    CLC                                                 ; test next character  $^$ 0xdfcc

.atEndOfCommandName
    BCS .foundMatchForCommand                           ;  $^$ 0xdfcd
    INX                                                 ; increment offset in star command table  $^$ 0xdfcf
    LDA (.stringInputBufferAddressLow),Y                ; read next character in command line  $^$ 0xdfd0
    JSR .isLetter                                       ; carry clear if letter in A  $^$ 0xdfd2
    BCC .compareCharacterInCommand                      ;  $^$ 0xdfd5

.lookForCommand
    LDA .starCommandTable,X                             ; read byte from command table  $^$ 0xdfd7
    BMI .endOfCommandStringFound                        ; if (top bit set, i.e. end of command name string) then branch  $^$ 0xdfda
    LDA (.stringInputBufferAddressLow),Y                ; read byte from command line  $^$ 0xdfdc
    CMP #.charDOT                                       ; check for '.'  $^$ 0xdfde
    BEQ .foundDot                                       ; if (dot character found) then branch  $^$ 0xdfe0

.namesDontMatch
    CLC                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdfe2
    LDY .currentStringPointer                           ;  $^$ 0xdfe3
    DEY                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdfe5

.foundDot
    INY                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdfe6
    INX                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdfe7

-
    INX                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdfe8
    LDA .starCommandTable-2,X                           ;  $^$ 0xdfe9
    BEQ .passCommandToROMs                              ; reached end of table; unrecognised star command  $^$ 0xdfec
    BPL -                                               ; if (top bit clear, i.e. not yet end of command name) then branch back (move to next character)  $^$ 0xdfee
    BMI .atEndOfCommandName                             ; ALWAYS branch (loop back)  $^$ 0xdff0

; ***************************************************************************************
.endOfCommandStringFound
    INX                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdff2
    INX                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdff3

.foundMatchForCommand
    DEX                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdff4
    DEX                                                 ;  $^$ 0xdff5
    PHA                                                 ; push star command address (high byte)  $^$ 0xdff6
    LDA .starCommandTable+1,X                           ;  get star command address (low byte)  $^$ 0xdff7
    PHA                                                 ; push star command address (low byte)  $^$ 0xdffa
    JSR .skipSpacesAndCheckForCRInStringInput           ; skip over the following spaces  $^$ 0xdffb
    CLC                                                 ; clear carry  $^$ 0xdffe
    PHP                                                 ; push flags  $^$ 0xdfff
    JSR .prepareRegistersForStarCommand                 ; prepare the A,X,Y registers for the call to star command routine  $^$ 0xe000

    ; the RTI instruction restores the flags, and jumps to the address we've just put on
    ; the stack. (i.e. jumps to the star command routine.)
    RTI                                                 ; jump to star command routine  $^$ 0xe003

; ***************************************************************************************
.prepareRegistersForStarCommand
    LDA .starCommandTable+2,X                           ; Get A parameter from table  $^$ 0xe004
    BMI .exit15                                         ; if (top bit set, this implies the  $^$ 0xe007
                                                        ; command has no string parameter, but
                                                        ; there may be numeric parameters)
                                                        ; then branch (exit, we are done)
                                                        ; otherwise we set XY to be the rest
                                                        ; of the command line (i.e. string
                                                        ; based)
    ; fall through...

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Convert string input pointer to XY
;
; On Entry:
;       X is the offset into the starCommandTable at the end of the string
;       Y is the offset into the string at .stringInputBufferAddressLow/High
;
; On Exit:
;       XY = (.stringInputBufferAddressLow/High + A)
;       A = parameter from star command table
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.convertStringInputPointerToXY
    TYA                                                 ; Pass Y line offset to A for later  $^$ 0xe009
    LDY .starCommandTable+2,X                           ; Get A parameter from table  $^$ 0xe00a
    ; fall through...

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Convert string address to XY
;
; On Entry:
;       A = is offset into string at .stringInputBufferAddressLow/High
;
; On Exit:
;       XY = .stringInputBufferAddressLow/High + A
;       A = original value of Y on entry
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.convertStringAddressToXY
    CLC                                                 ;  $^$ 0xe00d
    ADC .stringInputBufferAddressLow                    ;  $^$ 0xe00e
    TAX                                                 ; low byte in X  $^$ 0xe010
    TYA                                                 ; remember original Y into A  $^$ 0xe011
    LDY .stringInputBufferAddressHigh                   ; }  $^$ 0xe012
    BCC .exit15                                         ; } put high byte in Y, increment as needed  $^$ 0xe014
    INY                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xe016
.exit15
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xe017


; ***************************************************************************************
;
; *BASIC
;
; This command enters the BASIC language environment. The BASIC ROM is unique among Paged ROMs
; in not having a service entry. If it did, then the *BASIC command could be implemented in
; the BASIC ROM instead of here.
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.basicEntryPoint
    LDX .basicROMNumber                                 ; Get BASIC ROM number  $^$ 0xe018
    BMI .passCommandToROMs                              ; if (no BASIC found) then branch (pass command on to ROMs)  $^$ 0xe01b
    SEC                                                 ; Set Carry = not entering from RESET  $^$ 0xe01d
    JMP .osbyte142EntryPoint                            ; Enter language ROM in X  $^$ 0xe01e

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Pass command to ROMs
;
; Pass command on to Paged ROMs and to filing system
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.passCommandToROMs
    LDY .currentStringPointer                           ; Restore pointer to start of command  $^$ 0xe021
    LDX #.romServiceCallUnrecognisedCommand             ; 4 = Unrecognised star command  $^$ 0xe023
    JSR .osbyte143EntryPoint                            ; Pass to sideways ROMs  $^$ 0xe025
    BEQ .exit15                                         ; if (claimed by ROM) then branch (exit)  $^$ 0xe028
    LDA .currentStringPointer                           ; Restore pointer to start of command  $^$ 0xe02a
    JSR .convertStringAddressToXY                       ; Convert .stringInputBufferAddressLow/High+A to XY, ignore returned A  $^$ 0xe02c
    LDA #3                                              ; 3 = Auto-boot call  $^$ 0xe02f

.passToCurrentFilingSystem
    JMP (.vectorFSCV)                                   ; call into current filing system  $^$ 0xe031
                                                        ; handler (for default handler,
                                                        ; see .fscEntryPoint)

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; OSBYTE 139 - Select file options (*OPT)
;
; See .starOptEntryPoint for parameters
;
; On Entry:
;       X,Y hold the *OPT parameters
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.osbyte139EntryPoint
    ASL                                                 ; Double A (clear bit zero)  $^$ 0xe034
    ; fall through...

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; OSBYTE 127 - Check for EOF on open file
;
; On Entry:
;       X = file handle
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.osbyte127EntryPoint
    AND #1                                              ; A = 1 if entry via OSBYTE 127  $^$ 0xe035
                                                        ; A = 0 if entry via OSBYTE 139
    BPL .passToCurrentFilingSystem                      ; ALWAYS branch (send *OPT command  $^$ 0xe037
                                                        ; to the current filing system).

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Skip spaces
;
; On Entry:
;       .stringInputBufferAddressLow/High is address of string to test
;       Y is the current offset within the string
;
; On Exit:
;       Y is incremented to the next non-space character
;       Z set if RETURN found (end of string)
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.incAndSkipSpaces
    INY                                                 ; move to next character in string  $^$ 0xe039
.skipSpacesAndCheckForCRInStringInput
    LDA (.stringInputBufferAddressLow),Y                ; read character from string  $^$ 0xe03a
    CMP #.charSPACE                                     ; check for SPACE character  $^$ 0xe03c
    BEQ .incAndSkipSpaces                               ; if (SPACE) then branch (loop back)  $^$ 0xe03e
.compareWithReturnAndExit
    CMP #.charRETURN                                    ; set Z flag if charRETURN found  $^$ 0xe040
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xe042

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Skip spaces and comma
;
; Skip past any spaces, and check for CR
;
; On Entry:
;     if carry is clear, then skip SPACEs then look for RETURN
;     if carry is set, then skip SPACEs then skip a comma or look for a RETURN
;
; On Exit:
;       Y incremented past any spaces and comma
;       Z set if RETURN found
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.skipSpacesAndComma
    BCC .skipSpacesAndCheckForCRInStringInput           ; if (carry clear) then branch  $^$ 0xe043
.skipSpacesAndCommaValid
    JSR .skipSpacesAndCheckForCRInStringInput           ;  $^$ 0xe045
    CMP #.charCOMMA                                     ;  $^$ 0xe048
    BNE .compareWithReturnAndExit                       ;  $^$ 0xe04a
    INY                                                 ; move to next character. Y is not  $^$ 0xe04c
                                                        ; zero so Z is set.
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xe04d

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Read a number (0-255) from string
;
; On Entry:
;       stringInputBufferAddressLow/High + Y is address of string holding a number
; On Exit:
;       X = result (value 0-255) also stored in .tempWorkspaceE6
;       Carry clear on error
;       Zero set if RETURN found
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.parseDecimalNumberFromString
    JSR .skipSpacesAndCheckForCRInStringInput           ; skip spaces  $^$ 0xe04e
    JSR .readDigitFromString                            ; read digit  $^$ 0xe051
    BCC .errorReadingString                             ; if (error found) then branch (clear carry and exit)  $^$ 0xe054

.readingDigits
    STA .tempWorkspaceE6                                ; store temporary result  $^$ 0xe056
    JSR .readNextDigitFromString                        ; read next digit 0-9  $^$ 0xe058
    BCC .finishedParsingDigits                          ; if (not a digit) then branch (we have finished)  $^$ 0xe05b
    TAX                                                 ; remember best valid result so far  $^$ 0xe05d
    LDA .tempWorkspaceE6                                ; recall previous digit P  $^$ 0xe05e
    ASL                                                 ; A=P*2  $^$ 0xe060
    BCS .errorReadingString                             ; result too big, return with carry clear (error)  $^$ 0xe061
    ASL                                                 ; A=P*4  $^$ 0xe063
    BCS .errorReadingString                             ; result too big, return with carry clear (error)  $^$ 0xe064
    ADC .tempWorkspaceE6                                ; A=(P*4)+P =P*5  $^$ 0xe066
    BCS .errorReadingString                             ; result too big, return with carry clear (error)  $^$ 0xe068
    ASL                                                 ; A=P*10  $^$ 0xe06a
    BCS .errorReadingString                             ; result too big, return with carry clear (error)  $^$ 0xe06b
    STA .tempWorkspaceE6                                ; Store temporary result  $^$ 0xe06d
    TXA                                                 ; recall current digit  $^$ 0xe06f
    ADC .tempWorkspaceE6                                ; Add previous digit times ten  $^$ 0xe070
    BCS .errorReadingString                             ; result too big, return with carry clear (error)  $^$ 0xe072
    BCC .readingDigits                                  ; ALWAYS branch back  $^$ 0xe074

; ***************************************************************************************
.finishedParsingDigits
    LDX .tempWorkspaceE6                                ; get best valid result  $^$ 0xe076
    CMP #.charRETURN                                    ; set Z flag if RETURN found  $^$ 0xe078
    SEC                                                 ; set carry (success flag)  $^$ 0xe07a
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xe07b

; ***************************************************************************************
.readNextDigitFromString
    INY  $^$ 0xe07c
.readDigitFromString
    LDA (.stringInputBufferAddressLow),Y                ; get digit from string  $^$ 0xe07d
    CMP #.charNINE + 1                                  ; }  $^$ 0xe07f
    BCS .errorReadingString                             ; } check if digit is in range '0' to '9'  $^$ 0xe081
    CMP #.charZERO                                      ; }  $^$ 0xe083
    BCC .errorReadingString                             ; }  $^$ 0xe085
    AND #$0F                                            ; mask off bits to leave binary value 0-9  $^$ 0xe087
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xe089

; ***************************************************************************************
.notAHexByte
    JSR .skipSpacesAndCommaValid                        ;  $^$ 0xe08a

.errorReadingString
    CLC                                                 ;  $^$ 0xe08d
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xe08e

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Read hex digit
;
; On Exit:
;       on success, carry is set, A = 0-15, based on ascii digit in string (0-9,A-F)
;       on error, carry clear
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.readHexDigit
    JSR .readDigitFromString                            ; read digit 0-9  $^$ 0xe08f
    BCS +                                               ; if (digit not in 0-9 range) then branch  $^$ 0xe092
    AND #%11011111                                      ; clear bit 5 (converts lower case letters to upper case)  $^$ 0xe094
    CMP #.charF + 1                                     ;  $^$ 0xe096
    BCS .notAHexByte                                    ; if (higher than 'F') then branch (exit with error)  $^$ 0xe098
    CMP #.charA                                         ;  $^$ 0xe09a
    BCC .notAHexByte                                    ; if (lower than 'A') then branch (exit with error)  $^$ 0xe09c
    PHP                                                 ; carry set, push flags  $^$ 0xe09e
    SBC #.charA - 10                                    ; Convert to range 10-15  $^$ 0xe09f
    PLP                                                 ; restore flags (carry set, for successful result)  $^$ 0xe0a1
+
    INY                                                 ; move on to next byte  $^$ 0xe0a2
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xe0a3


; ***************************************************************************************
; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Chapter 13: Writing characters; printer; buffers
;
; ***************************************************************************************
; ***************************************************************************************
