    TAY                                                 ; Y=A  $^$ 0xfba2
                                                        ; now, Y = 1 for input
                                                        ;      Y = 2 for output
    LDA .fsStatusByte                                   ; tape / ROM FS status byte  $^$ 0xfba3
    AND .fsTempStorage                                  ; file status or temporary store  $^$ 0xfba5
    LSR                                                 ; set carry if open for input  $^$ 0xfba7
    DEY                                                 ; Y = Y - 1  $^$ 0xfba8
    BEQ +                                               ; if (checking open for input) then branch  $^$ 0xfba9
    LSR                                                 ; set carry if open for output  $^$ 0xfbab
    DEY                                                 ; Y = Y - 1  $^$ 0xfbac
    BNE .channelError                                   ; if (not checking open for output) then branch  $^$ 0xfbad
+
    BCS .exit36                                         ; if (file is open as expected) then branch (exit)  $^$ 0xfbaf

.channelError
    BRK                                                 ;  $^$ 0xfbb1
    !byte $DE                                           ; error number
    !text "Channel"                                     ; message
    !byte 0                                             ; terminator

; ***************************************************************************************
; See NAUG Section 18.8, Page 340
.startSendToSecondProcessor
    LDA #1                                              ; A=1 (Multiple single byte transfer:  $^$ 0xfbbb
                                                        ; main processor to second processor)
.secondProcessorTransfer
    JSR .checkLoadAddressIsForSecondProcessor           ; check if load address is valid  $^$ 0xfbbd
    BEQ .exit36                                         ; if (load address is for main processor) then branch (exit)  $^$ 0xfbc0
    TXA                                                 ; A=1  $^$ 0xfbc2
    LDX #<.loadAddressLow                               ; }  $^$ 0xfbc3
    LDY #>.loadAddressLow                               ; } set up parameter block address  $^$ 0xfbc5
.secondProcessorCall
    PHA                                                 ; save A=1 on stack  $^$ 0xfbc7
    LDA #.tubeClaimReasonCode + .tubeCallerIDCassetteFS ; Claim the Tube, caller is the  $^$ 0xfbc8
                                                        ; Cassette Filing System
-
    JSR .tubeTransferData                               ; call out to Tube  $^$ 0xfbca
    BCC -                                               ; keep trying to claim until claim is done  $^$ 0xfbcd
    PLA                                                 ; pull A=1 (Multiple single byte  $^$ 0xfbcf
                                                        ; transfer: main processor to second
                                                        ; processor)
    JMP .tubeTransferData                               ;  $^$ 0xfbd0

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Check load address for destination
;
; Check the top two bytes of the 32 bit load address. If they are both $FF, then it is for
; the main processor and we return with Z set. If the Tube is not present, then we also
; return with Z set. Otherwise it's for the Tube, we return with Z clear.
;
; On Exit:
;       Z set if load address is for the second processor
;       X is value of A on entry
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.checkLoadAddressIsForSecondProcessor
    TAX                                                 ; X=A  $^$ 0xfbd3
    LDA .loadAddressMid2                                ; current load address high word  $^$ 0xfbd4
    AND .loadAddressHigh                                ; current load address high word  $^$ 0xfbd6
    CMP #$FF                                            ;  $^$ 0xfbd8
    BEQ +                                               ; if ($FF, i.e. it's for base processor) then branch  $^$ 0xfbda
    LDA .tubePresentFlag                                ; $FF if Tube is present  $^$ 0xfbdc
    AND #%10000000                                      ; Set bit 7 alone if Tube is present  $^$ 0xfbdf
+
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xfbe1

; ***************************************************************************************
; This routine is actually a bugfix. Commented from the original source code:
;
; BUGFIX
;
; When the 6850 counter divide bits are reset, it is possible for the SERPROC to get out
; of synch. for a few bits. This has the effect of corrupting the first character of the
; first block of a SAVE, or the first character of ANY block during sequential access
; (since the 6850 is reset for every block during putbytes).
;
; The cure is to write a dummy byte to tape at the start of a SAVE, and at the start of
; every block during putbytes. This must be done by polling, since there must be a period
; of high-tone after the dummy byte, which is difficult to accomplish if the 6850 is
; interrupting all the time. BUGFIX is thus called after the SERPROC is set and before the
; 6850 is set to interrupt during a block write operation.
;
; ["SERPROC" refers to .serialULAControlRegister, and "BUGFIX" is this routine]
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.setupForCassetteWrite
    LDA #%10000101                                      ; } switch on the cassette motor and relay  $^$ 0xfbe2
    STA .serialULAControlRegister                       ; } and set 300 baud  $^$ 0xfbe4
    JSR .resetACIA                                      ; reset ACIA  $^$ 0xfbe7
    LDA #%00010000                                      ; } even parity  $^$ 0xfbea
                                                        ; } 2 stop bits
                                                        ; } 8 bit word
                                                        ; } 'Request To Send' ('RTS') low (active)
                                                        ; } disable interrupts
    JSR .setACIA6850ControlRegister                     ; set ACIA to tape filing system baud rate  $^$ 0xfbec

-
    JSR .checkForEscapeDuringCassetteOperation          ; check for ESCAPE  $^$ 0xfbef
    LDA .acia6850StatusRegister                         ; read ACIA status register  $^$ 0xfbf2
    AND #%00000010                                      ; check bit 1 (transmit interrupt generated)  $^$ 0xfbf5
    BEQ -                                               ; if (bit 1 clear, i.e. transmit  $^$ 0xfbf7
                                                        ; interrupt generated) then branch
                                                        ; (loop back and try again)

    LDA #%10101010                                      ; A=$AA  $^$ 0xfbf9
    STA .acia6850DataRegister                           ; send byte to tape  $^$ 0xfbfb
.exit36
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xfbfe

    !byte 0                                             ; [unused]

; Chapter 23: Extended vectors

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Extended Vector Entry Points
;
; ***************************************************************************************
; See NAUG Section 17.4.3 - Extended Vectors, Page 312
;
; There is a mechanism by which Paged ROMs can intercept the standard vectors at $0200
; upwards, instead getting them to point to a specific address *in a specified ROM*.
;
; To intercept vector N:
;
;   - Disable interrupts during this change over
;   - Get memory base address (call it V) using OSBYTE 168
;           (V is address '.extendedVectorSpace' in this particular version of the ROM)
;   - Store desired ROM address for routine at the two byte starting at V+3*N
;   - Store desired ROM number in the following byte
;   - Make a copy of the original contents of the vector at $0200+2*N if needed
;   - Store the address '$FF00+3*N' in OS vector at '$0200+2*N'
;
.extendedVectorTable
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_USERV  $^$ 0xff00
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_BRKV  $^$ 0xff03
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_IRQ1V  $^$ 0xff06
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_IRQ2V  $^$ 0xff09
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_CLIV  $^$ 0xff0c
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_BYTEV  $^$ 0xff0f
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_WORDV  $^$ 0xff12
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_WRCHV  $^$ 0xff15
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_RDCHV  $^$ 0xff18
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_FILEV  $^$ 0xff1b
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_ARGSV  $^$ 0xff1e
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_BGETV  $^$ 0xff21
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_BPUTV  $^$ 0xff24
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_GBPBV  $^$ 0xff27
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_FINDV  $^$ 0xff2a
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_FSCV  $^$ 0xff2d
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_EVENTV  $^$ 0xff30
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_UPTV  $^$ 0xff33
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_NETV  $^$ 0xff36
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_VDUV  $^$ 0xff39
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_KEYV  $^$ 0xff3c
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_INSV  $^$ 0xff3f
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_REMV  $^$ 0xff42
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_CNPV  $^$ 0xff45
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_IND1V  $^$ 0xff48
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_IND2V  $^$ 0xff4b
    JSR .extendedVectorEntryPoint                       ; E_IND3V  $^$ 0xff4e

; ***************************************************************************************
.extendedVectorEntryPoint
    PHA                                                 ; save A on stack - make space for currently selected ROM (address '$109,X' in code below)  $^$ 0xff51
    PHA                                                 ; save A on stack - make space for return address low     (address '$108,X' in code below)  $^$ 0xff52
    PHA                                                 ; save A on stack - make space for return address high    (address '$107,X' in code below)  $^$ 0xff53
    PHA                                                 ; save A on stack - make space for ROM address low        (address '$106,X' in code below)  $^$ 0xff54
    PHA                                                 ; save A on stack - make space for ROM address high       (address '$105,X' in code below)  $^$ 0xff55

    PHP                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff56
    PHA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff57
    TXA                                                 ; } save Flags,A,X,Y to the stack  $^$ 0xff58
    PHA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff59
    TYA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff5a
    PHA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff5b
    TSX                                                 ; get stack pointer into X  $^$ 0xff5c

    LDA #>(.returnFromROM-1)                            ; }  $^$ 0xff5d
    STA .stackPage + 8,X                                ; }  $^$ 0xff5f
    LDA #<(.returnFromROM-1)                            ; } store return address in the stack (the .returnFromROM routine below)  $^$ 0xff62
    STA .stackPage + 7,X                                ; }  $^$ 0xff64

    LDY .stackPage + 10,X                               ; Y=3*N+2 (low byte of caller address)  $^$ 0xff67
    LDA .extendedVectorSpace-2,Y                        ; get low byte of action address  $^$ 0xff6a
    STA .stackPage + 5,X                                ; store it on stack  $^$ 0xff6d
    LDA .extendedVectorSpace-1,Y                        ; get high byte of action address  $^$ 0xff70
    STA .stackPage + 6,X                                ; store it on stack  $^$ 0xff73
    LDA .currentlySelectedROM                           ; get the current ROM number  $^$ 0xff76
    STA .stackPage + 9,X                                ; store it on stack  $^$ 0xff78
    LDA .extendedVectorSpace,Y                          ; get new ROM number  $^$ 0xff7b
    STA .currentlySelectedROM                           ; store RAM copy of current ROM  $^$ 0xff7e
    STA .romSelectRegister                              ; switch the ROM into the memory map  $^$ 0xff80
    PLA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff83
    TAY                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff84
    PLA                                                 ; } Restore Y,X,A from stack  $^$ 0xff85
    TAX                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff86
    PLA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff87

    RTI                                                 ; the RTI instruction restores the  $^$ 0xff88
                                                        ; flags, and jumps to the (ROM)
                                                        ; address we've put on the stack.
                                                        ; i.e. this jumps to the ROM routine.
                                                        ; When that returns, the address on
                                                        ; the stack jumps us to the routine
                                                        ; below.

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Return from ROM
;
; Once the ROM routine from above is finished, the return address takes us here, which restores
; the registers and returns to the proper calling routine.
;
.returnFromROM
    PHP                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff89
    PHA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff8a
    TXA                                                 ; } save Flags,A,X to the stack  $^$ 0xff8b
    PHA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff8c
    TSX                                                 ;  $^$ 0xff8d
    LDA .stackPage + 2,X                                ; }  $^$ 0xff8e
    STA .stackPage + 5,X                                ; }  $^$ 0xff91
    LDA .stackPage + 3,X                                ; } store real return address onto stack (ready for RTS)  $^$ 0xff94
    STA .stackPage + 6,X                                ; }  $^$ 0xff97

    PLA                                                 ; }  $^$ 0xff9a
    TAX                                                 ; } recall X  $^$ 0xff9b
    PLA                                                 ; recall A - lose these 2 bytes. They are the address of this routine.  $^$ 0xff9c
    PLA                                                 ; recall A - lose these 2 bytes. They are the address of this routine.  $^$ 0xff9d
    PLA                                                 ; get back A (original ROM number)  $^$ 0xff9e
    STA .currentlySelectedROM                           ; store it as RAM copy of current ROM number  $^$ 0xff9f
    STA .romSelectRegister                              ; switch the ROM into the memory map  $^$ 0xffa1

    PLA                                                 ; get back A  $^$ 0xffa4
    PLP                                                 ; get back flags  $^$ 0xffa5
.return
    RTS                                                 ; return (pulls real return address from stack)  $^$ 0xffa6


; ***************************************************************************************
; ***************************************************************************************

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; OSBYTE 157 - Fast Tube BPUT
;
; By default this uses the standard OSBPUT routine.
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.osbyte157EntryPoint
    TXA                                                 ; A=X  $^$ 0xff58
    BCS .OSBPUT                                         ; ALWAYS branch  $^$ 0xffa8

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; OSBYTE 146 - Read a byte from FRED
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.osbyte146EntryPoint
    LDY .fredPage,X                                     ; read a byte from FRED area  $^$ 0xffaa
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xffad

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; OSBYTE 148 - Read a byte from JIM
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.osbyte148EntryPoint
    LDY .jimPage,X                                      ; read a byte from JIM area  $^$ 0xffae
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xffb1

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; OSBYTE 150 - Read a byte from SHEILA
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.osbyte150EntryPoint
    LDY .sheilaPage,X                                   ; read a byte from SHEILA area  $^$ 0xffb2
    RTS                                                 ;  $^$ 0xffb5

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Default vector table pointer
;
; User programs can read these locations to find the default handler addresses.
; It is not well documented (it's not in the NAUG), but it does appear in the Electron
; Advanced User Guide section 6.11. It is not used by this ROM. New in MOS 1.20.
;
; The original source code has the cryptic comment "security copy of indirection data"
;
; ***************************************************************************************
    !byte .defaultVectorTableEnd - .defaultVectorTable  ; length of table         [unused]
    !word .defaultVectorTable                           ; table of addresses - the
                                                        ; default vector routines [unused]

; ***************************************************************************************
;
; Operating System function calls
;
; Historical note: The Acorn System 2 began the practice of placing entry points like
; these at the high end of the ROM, (mostly) spaced three bytes apart so that each can
; jump directly back into the ROM or through a vector, and still be called as if they
; were subroutines. This practice protected user programs from breaking when the MOS was
; revised, since it meant there were reliable addresses to call. Though System 2, and
; similarly the Atom, have a slightly smaller set of entry points, so addresses are not
; the same (OSWRCH is at $FFF4 on the System 2 and Atom, not $FFEE as here), the basic
; design is identical. System 2 and the Atom both perform the CR/LF manoeuvre below in
; which OSASCI, OSNEWL and OSWRCH are combined.
;
; ***************************************************************************************
.OSRDRM
    JMP .osrdrmEntryPoint                               ; get a byte from sideways ROM [new in MOS 1.20]  $^$ 0xffb9
.VDUCHR
    JMP .vduChrEntryPoint                               ; output a character to screen  $^$ 0xffbc
.OSEVEN
    JMP .eventEntryPoint                                ; generate an EVENT  $^$ 0xffbf
.GSINIT
    JMP .gsinitEntryPoint                               ; initialise for parsing a string  $^$ 0xffc2
.GSREAD
    JMP .gsreadEntryPoint                               ; parse character from string  $^$ 0xffc5
.NVRDCH
    JMP .osrdchEntryPoint                               ; non vectored .OSRDCH  $^$ 0xffc8
.NVWRCH
    JMP .oswrchEntryPoint                               ; non vectored .OSWRCH  $^$ 0xffcb
.OSFIND
    JMP (.vectorFINDV)                                  ; open or close a file  $^$ 0xffce
.OSGBPB
    JMP (.vectorGBPBV)                                  ; transfer data to or from a file  $^$ 0xffd1
.OSBPUT
    JMP (.vectorBPUTV)                                  ; save a byte to file  $^$ 0xffd4
.OSBGET
    JMP (.vectorBGETV)                                  ; get a byte from file  $^$ 0xffd7
.OSARGS
    JMP (.vectorARGSV)                                  ; read or write file arguments  $^$ 0xffda
.OSFILE
    JMP (.vectorFILEV)                                  ; read or write a file  $^$ 0xffdd
.OSRDCH
    JMP (.vectorRDCHV)                                  ; get byte from current input stream  $^$ 0xffe0
.OSASCI
    CMP #.charRETURN                                    ; output byte, expanding carriage  $^$ 0xffe3
    BNE .OSWRCH                                         ; returns to CR/LF ($0A,$0D)  $^$ 0xffe5
.OSNEWL
    LDA #.charLINEFEED                                  ; output a CR/LF to VDU stream  $^$ 0xffe7
    JSR .OSWRCH                                         ;  $^$ 0xffe9
    LDA #.charRETURN                                    ;  $^$ 0xffec
.OSWRCH
    JMP (.vectorWRCHV)                                  ; output a character (to the screen  $^$ 0xffee
                                                        ; and/or other output streams)
.OSWORD
    JMP (.vectorWORDV)                                  ; perform operation with data from  $^$ 0xfff1
                                                        ; a parameter table
.OSBYTE
    JMP (.vectorBYTEV)                                  ; perform operation with three  $^$ 0xfff4
                                                        ; parameters <A>,<X>,<Y>
                                                        ; (equivalent to BASIC's *FX command)
.OSCLI
    JMP (.vectorCLIV)                                   ; pass string to command line  $^$ 0xfff7
                                                        ; interpreter


; ***************************************************************************************
;
; 6502 Vectors
;
; See 6502.png
;
; Finally the last 6 bytes are designated (by the design of the 6502 chip) to contain the
; addresses of the routines that handle an NMI, a RESET and an IRQ condition.
;
; ***************************************************************************************
* = $FFFA
    !word .nmiEntryPoint                                ; NMI   address
    !word .resetEntryPoint                              ; RESET address
    !word .irqEntryPoint                                ; IRQ   address

;
; OSWORD
;
; See .oswordEntryPoint
;
; OSWORD   0 - Read line from current input into memory     See .osword0EntryPoint

; OSWORD   2 - Write system clock                           See .osword2EntryPoint
; OSWORD   3 - Read interval timer                          See .osword3EntryPoint
; OSWORD   4 - Write interval timer                         See .osword4EntryPoint
; OSWORD   5 - Read a byte from I/O memory                  See .osword5EntryPoint
; OSWORD   6 - Write a byte to I/O memory                   See .osword6EntryPoint
; OSWORD   7 - Make a sound                                 See .osword7EntryPoint
; OSWORD   8 - Define an envelope                           See .osword8EntryPoint
; OSWORD   9 - Read a pixel                                 See .osword9EntryPoint
; OSWORD  10 - Read character definition                    See .osword10EntryPoint
; OSWORD  11 - Read palette                                 See .osword11EntryPoint
; OSWORD  12 - Write palette                                See .osword12EntryPoint
; OSWORD  13 - Read last two graphic cursor positions       See .osword13EntryPoint
;
; OSWORDs 14-255 are undefined.
; OSWORDs 224-255 are routed through USERV.
;

;
; OS Entry Points
;
; OS Call       Vector             Default handler         Description
; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
; See .GSINIT   -                  See .gsinitEntryPoint   Initialise for parsing a string
; See .GSREAD   -                  See .gsreadEntryPoint   Parse a character from string
; See .NVRDCH   -                  See .osrdchEntryPoint   Non-vectored .OSRDCH
; See .NVWRCH   -                  See .oswrchEntryPoint   Non-vectored .OSWRCH
; See .OSARGS   See .vectorARGSV   See .osargsEntryPoint   Read or write file arguments
; See .OSASCI   -                  See .OSASCI             Output byte, expanding CR
; See .OSBGET   See .vectorBGETV   See .osbgetEntryPoint   Get a byte from file
; See .OSBPUT   See .vectorBPUTV   See .osbputEntryPoint   Save a byte to file
; See .OSBYTE   See .vectorBYTEV   See .osbyteEntryPoint   OS call with A,X,Y parameters
; See .OSCLI    See .vectorCLIV    See .oscliEntryPoint    Execute star command string
; See .OSEVEN   -                  See .eventEntryPoint    Generate an EVENT
; See .OSFILE   See .vectorFILEV   See .osfileEntryPoint   Read or write a file
; See .OSFIND   See .vectorFINDV   See .osfindEntryPoint   Open or close a file
; See .OSGBPB   See .vectorGBPBV   -                       Transfer block to or from a file
; See .OSNEWL   -                  See .OSNEWL             Output CR/LF
; See .OSRDCH   See .vectorRDCHV   See .osrdchEntryPoint   Get byte from current input stream
; See .OSRDRM   -                  See .osrdrmEntryPoint   Get a byte from sideways ROM
; See .OSWORD   See .vectorWORDV   See .oswordEntryPoint   OS call with parameter block
; See .OSWRCH   See .vectorWRCHV   See .oswrchEntryPoint   Output a character
; See .VDUCHR   -                  See .vduChrEntryPoint   Output a character to screen
;
